_meta.title: Declarative Pipeline grammar dictionary
purpose: A machine-readable dictionary of the identifiers that are legal in a Jenkins
Declarative Pipeline: the directives (which are a CLOSED set defined by the
pipeline-model-definition plugin's own grammar) and the steps (which are an
OPEN set - every plugin contributes more).
This file exists so that the claims scripted_to_declarative.py makes about
Declarative syntax are auditable data rather than knowledge baked into prose
and code comments. It follows the same rule as the converter itself: nothing
in here is written from memory or inferred. Every identifier below was read
off Jenkins's own documentation, and anything that could not be verified there
is listed under `unverified` rather than being quietly included.

open: steps - any plugin can contribute a step, and Declarative does NOT validate
step NAMES, only statement SHAPE. `steps.core` below is therefore a grounded
subset (the steps shipped by the standard Pipeline plugins), never a whitelist.
Do not use it to reject a step you do not recognise.

structural_rules: A `stage` must have one and only one of `steps`, `stages`, `parallel`, or `matrix`.
It is not possible to nest a `parallel` or `matrix` block within a `stage` directive if that `stage` directive is itself nested within a `parallel` or `matrix` block.
A `steps` block may contain only step invocations - not assignments, not if/for/while/try/switch, not bare expressions. `script` is the documented escape hatch for those.

The 'must be a step' rule applies only to what `steps` directly enumerates. Groovy nested inside a step's own closure argument (dir, withEnv, timeout, retry, catchError, script, ...) is ordinary CPS Groovy and is not restricted.
`@Library('x') _` is a compile-time annotation and belongs ABOVE the `pipeline` block, never inside it.

sections._note: Directives valid directly inside the top-level `pipeline` block.
sections.pipeline: The outermost block. Required; everything else nests inside it.
sections.agent: Where the pipeline (or stage) executes. Required at top level.
sections.stages: Container for one or more `stage` blocks. Required at top level.
sections.post: Steps run at the end of the pipeline (or stage), keyed by build result.
sections.environment: Key/value environment variables. Valid at pipeline AND stage level.
sections.parameters: Build parameters prompted for at trigger time (see `parameters`).
sections.tools: Tools to auto-install and put on the PATH (see `tools`).

stage_directives.agent: Per-stage agent; overrides the pipeline agent.
stage_directives.input: Pause and prompt for input before the stage runs (see `input`).
stage_directives.when: Condition determining whether the stage runs (see `when`).
stage_directives.steps: The stage's steps. Mutually exclusive with stages/parallel/matrix.
stage_directives.stages: Sequential nested stages. Mutually exclusive with steps/parallel/matrix.
stage_directives.parallel: Parallel nested stages. Mutually exclusive with steps/stages/matrix.
stage_directives.matrix: Matrix of stages over one or more axes. Mutually exclusive with steps/stages/parallel.

types.none: No global agent; every stage must declare its own.
types.label: Run on an agent matching the label.
types.node: Like `label`, but allows additional options such as customWorkspace.
types.dockerfile: Build an image from a Dockerfile in the repo and run inside it.

common_options.label: Agent label to run on.
common_options.customWorkspace: Run in a specific workspace directory.
common_options.reuseNode: Reuse the workspace/node from the top-level agent instead of allocating a new one.

dockerfile_options.dir: Directory containing the Dockerfile, for a non-root build context.
dockerfile_options.label: Agent label on which to build and run the container.

kubernetes_options.defaultContainer: Container in the pod to run steps in by default.

post_conditions.always: Run regardless of the completion status.
post_conditions.changed: Run only if the current run's status differs from the previous run's.
post_conditions.fixed: Run only if the current run succeeded and the previous run failed or was unstable.
post_conditions.regression: Run only if the current run's status is worse than the previous run's.
post_conditions.aborted: Run only if the run was aborted.
post_conditions.failure: Run only if the run failed.
post_conditions.success: Run only if the run succeeded.
post_conditions.unstable: Run only if the run was unstable.
post_conditions.unsuccessful: Run only if the run was not successful.
post_conditions.cleanup: Run after every other post condition, regardless of status.

pipeline.checkoutToSubdirectory: Check out to a subdirectory of the workspace.
pipeline.disableConcurrentBuilds: Prevent concurrent executions of the pipeline.
pipeline.disableResume: Do not resume the pipeline if the controller restarts.
pipeline.newContainerPerStage: With a docker/dockerfile agent, run each stage in a new container.
pipeline.preserveStashes: Preserve stashes from completed builds, for stage restarts.
pipeline.quietPeriod: Quiet period, in seconds, for the pipeline.
pipeline.retry: Retry the whole pipeline the given number of times on failure.
pipeline.skipDefaultCheckout: Skip the implicit `checkout scm` in `agent` directives.
pipeline.skipStagesAfterUnstable: Skip remaining stages once the build is unstable.
pipeline.timeout: Timeout for the whole pipeline, after which it is aborted.
pipeline.parallelsAlwaysFailFast: Apply failFast to every parallel stage in the pipeline.
pipeline.disableRestartFromStage: Disable restarting the pipeline from a stage.

stage.skipDefaultCheckout: Skip the implicit `checkout scm` for this stage.
stage.retry: Retry this stage the given number of times on failure.
stage.timestamps: Prepend timestamps to this stage's console output.

parallel.failFast: Abort all parallel branches as soon as one fails. Written `failFast true` inside the stage containing the `parallel` block.

parameters.choice: Choice parameter, selected from a list.

triggers.pollSCM: Poll the SCM on a cron-style schedule.
triggers.upstream: Run when an upstream job completes with a given result.

conditions.branch: Run when the branch name matches. Supports a `comparator`.
conditions.changelog: Run when the changelog matches a regular expression.
conditions.changeset: Run when the changeset contains matching files. Supports `comparator` and `caseSensitive`.
conditions.changeRequest: Run when building a change request (PR/MR). Supports a `comparator`.
conditions.environment: Run when an environment variable has a given value.
conditions.equals: Run when the expected value equals the actual value.
conditions.expression: Run when the Groovy expression evaluates true.
conditions.tag: Run when the tag name matches. Supports a `comparator`.
conditions.allOf: Run when all nested conditions are true.
conditions.anyOf: Run when any nested condition is true.
conditions.triggeredBy: Run when the build was triggered by the given cause.

evaluation_options.beforeAgent: Evaluate the `when` condition before entering the agent.
evaluation_options.beforeInput: Evaluate the `when` condition before the `input` directive.
evaluation_options.beforeOptions: Evaluate the `when` condition before the stage `options`.

matrix.name: Name of an axis (inside `axis`) or of an excluded axis (inside `exclude`).
matrix.exclude: One excluded combination of axis values.
matrix.stages: The stages run for every cell of the matrix.

input.message: Prompt shown to the user. Required.
input.id: Identifier for the input, defaulting to the stage name.
input.submitterParameter: Environment variable to populate with the submitter's name.
input.parameters: Parameters prompted for alongside the input.

tools._note: Tool types documented on the syntax page. A tool must also be configured under Manage Jenkins > Tools.

environment._note: Valid inside the `pipeline` block or within `stage` directives.

credentials._description: Special helper method accessing pre-defined Credentials by identifier.
credentials.Secret Text: The variable is set to the secret text content.
credentials.Secret File: The variable is set to the location of a temporarily created file.
credentials.Username and password: The variable is set to `username:password`, and MYVARNAME_USR and MYVARNAME_PSW are also defined.
credentials.SSH with Private Key: The variable is set to the location of a temporarily created key file, and MYVARNAME_USR and MYVARNAME_PSW (the passphrase) are also defined.

_note: OPEN SET. Declarative does not validate step names - any plugin can add a step,
and a call to a function you defined yourself is equally legal. The lists below
are the steps shipped by the standard Pipeline plugins, grounded in the plugin
documentation, and exist for reference and tooling hints - NOT as a whitelist.
`block: true` marks a step that takes a closure body. That distinction is the
one that matters most when converting Scripted to Declarative: a block step is
copied through as a single statement, and the Groovy inside its closure is not
subject to the 'must be a step' rule.

script.desc: Run arbitrary Pipeline script - the escape hatch for non-step Groovy inside steps.

validateDeclarativePipeline.desc: Validate a file containing a Declarative Pipeline.

envVarsForTool.desc: Fetch the environment variables for a given tool as a list of 'FOO=bar' strings.

catchError.desc: Catch error and set build result to failure.

deleteDir.desc: Recursively delete the current directory from the workspace.

fileExists.desc: Verify if file exists in workspace.

isUnix.desc: Check if running on a Unix-like node.

retry.desc: Retry the body up to N times.

stash.desc: Stash some files to be used later in the build.

step.desc: Invoke a general build step from freestyle or similar projects.

tool.desc: Use a tool from a predefined Tool Installation.

warnError.desc: Catch error and set build and stage result to unstable.

wrap.desc: Apply a build wrapper around a block.

getContext.desc: Get contextual object from internal APIs.

unarchive.desc: Copy archived artifacts into the workspace.

withContext.desc: Use contextual object from internal APIs within a block.

dir.desc: Change current directory for the body.

node.desc: Allocate an executor and workspace on a node. SCRIPTED ONLY at pipeline level - in Declarative this is expressed as `agent`.

powershell.desc: Execute a Windows PowerShell script (version 3 or later).

sh.desc: Run a Bourne shell script, typically on a Unix node.

ws.desc: Allocate a workspace, optionally in a specific directory.

load.desc: Evaluate a Groovy source file into the Pipeline script.

parallel.desc: Execute in parallel. Takes a map of branch name to closure; in Declarative there is also a `parallel` DIRECTIVE, which is different.

library.desc: Load a shared library dynamically at runtime. Arguments: `identifier` (e.g. 'my-lib@master'), and optionally `retriever`. The compile-time alternative is the `@Library` annotation above the pipeline block.

shared_libraries._note: Not a Declarative directive - `@Library` is a Groovy ANNOTATION, resolved when the Jenkinsfile is compiled, so it must appear above the `pipeline` block in Declarative exactly as in Scripted.
step_forms: library identifier: 'custom-lib@master', retriever: modernSCM([$class: 'GitSCMSource', remote: '...', credentialsId: '...'])

_note: Identifiers that are widely used in the wild but that could NOT be confirmed on
the Jenkins documentation pages listed in _meta.sources on the verification date.
They are recorded here rather than in the dictionary proper so that nothing above
is asserted without a source. Check them against the plugin versions you actually
run - e.g. with the declarative-linter - before relying on them.
unverified.libraries: A `libraries { lib('my-lib@master') }` directive is commonly attributed to the pipeline-model-definition plugin, but does not appear on the Declarative syntax page, the Shared Libraries page, or the plugin's own step reference. Use the `@Library` annotation, which is documented.
unverified.isRestartedRun: Sometimes listed as a `when` condition. Does not appear in the built-in conditions on the syntax page.
